Erreur : Invalid pattern '(\d+' at offset 4. Not enough )'s.
Tapez le modèle à tester ou rien pour arrêter :

The templates [^\s*\d+\s*$] and [^\s*(\d+)\s*$] demonstrate the usefulness of groups: the first recognizes the string “1456” preceded by three spaces, including the spaces; the second additionally extracts the number without the spaces. The [(a+)+$] template is examined below.

docs.title: 5.8.5. The Split Method
docs.text:
We have already encountered the [Split] method from the [String] class:

methodrole[public string[] Split(params char[] separator)]The string is treated as a sequence of fields separated by the characters listed in the array [separator]. The result is an array of these fields

The method [Split] of the class [Regex] allows us to specify the separator using a pattern:

methodrole[public string[] Split(string input)]The string [input] is split into fields, which are separated by a separator corresponding to the pattern of the current [Regex] object

Suppose, for example, that a text file contains lines of the form field1, field2, ..., fieldn. The fields are separated by a comma, but this comma may be preceded or followed by spaces. The [\s*,\s*] template describes this separator exactly, as shown by the [regex-05.cs] program:

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

// Regex.Split: the separator is defined by a template
string ligne = "abc  , def  ,ghi ,   jkl";
// a comma preceded and followed by any number of spaces
var separateur = new Regex(@"\s*,\s*");
string[] champs = separateur.Split(ligne);
for (int i = 0; i < champs.Length; i++)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"champs[{i}]=[{champs[i]}]");
}
// several possible separators: ; or | or a sequence of spaces
string[] mots = Regex.Split("un;deux|trois   quatre", @"[;|]|\s+");
Console.WriteLine($"mots=[{string.Join(", ", mots)}]");

Results:

> dotnet run regex-05.cs
champs[0]=[abc]
champs[1]=[def]
champs[2]=[ghi]
champs[3]=[jkl]
mots=[un, deux, trois, quatre]

Comments:

  • line 6: the separator: a comma preceded and followed by any number of spaces. The spaces are removed along with the separator. Note that the option [TrimEntries] from [string.Split], presented above, now allows you to achieve the same result without a regular expression;
  • Line 13: A separator that can take several forms: a semicolon or a vertical bar ([;|]), or ([|]) a sequence of spaces ([\s+]). Here, a regular expression is required.

docs.title: 5.8.6. Generated regular expressions, options, timeout
docs.text:
A [Regex] object parses its template at runtime, then translates it into an internal structure that it interprets, or compiles into executable code if the [RegexOptions.Compiled] option is passed to it. Starting with .NET 7, the [GeneratedRegex] attribute allows this work to be done at compile time: a source generator writes the C# code for the search, which can be viewed in the editor (F12 on the method). The template is validated at compile time, there is no longer any analysis overhead at startup, and the generated code runs as fast as possible. This is now the recommended way to use a template known in advance. The program [regex-06.cs] is as follows:

using System.Diagnostics;
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

// 1 - regular expressions generated at compile time
Console.WriteLine($"Heure(\"Il est 18:05:49\") : {Modeles.Heure().IsMatch("Il est 18:05:49")}");
Match m = Modeles.Heure().Match("départ à 07:45:00");
Console.WriteLine($"heures={m.Groups["h"].Value}, minutes={m.Groups["m"].Value}, secondes={m.Groups["s"].Value}");

// 2 - options: here IgnoreCase, specified in the attribute
foreach (string reponse in new[] { "oui", "OUI", "Oui", "non", "ouiii" })
{
    Console.Write($"{reponse}={Modeles.Oui().IsMatch(reponse)} ");
}
Console.WriteLine();
// Options are combined with |: Multiline matches ^ and $ at the beginning and end of each line
string texte = "prix: 10\nquantité: 3\ntotal: 30";
foreach (Match ligne in Regex.Matches(texte, @"^(\w+): (\d+)$", RegexOptions.Multiline))
{
    Console.Write($"[{ligne.Groups[1].Value}={ligne.Groups[2].Value}] ");
}
Console.WriteLine();

// 3 - A timeout protects against templates with catastrophic backspace behavior
string chaine = new string('a', 30) + "!";
try
{
    Console.WriteLine(Modeles.Catastrophe().IsMatch(chaine));
}
catch (RegexMatchTimeoutException e)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{e.GetType().Name} : recherche abandonnée au bout de {e.MatchTimeout.TotalMilliseconds} ms");
}
// The same pattern with the no-backspace engine responds immediately
var chrono = Stopwatch.StartNew();
bool trouve = Regex.IsMatch(chaine, @"^(a+)+$", RegexOptions.NonBacktracking);
Console.WriteLine($"NonBacktracking : {trouve}, réponse en moins d'une seconde : {chrono.ElapsedMilliseconds < 1000}");

// the program's patterns
static partial class Modeles
{
     // a time in hh:mm:ss format with named groups
    [GeneratedRegex(@"(?<h>\d\d):(?<m>\d\d):(?<s>\d\d)")]
    public static partial Regex Heure();

     // Yes, regardless of case
    [GeneratedRegex(@"^\s*oui\s*$", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase)]
    public static partial Regex Oui();

     // a pathological model, with a timeout of 100 ms
    [GeneratedRegex(@"^(a+)+$", RegexOptions.None, matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 100)]
    public static partial Regex Catastrophe();
}

Results:

> dotnet run regex-06.cs
Heure("Il est 18:05:49") : True
heures=07, minutes=45, secondes=00
oui=True OUI=True Oui=True non=False ouiii=False 
[prix=10] [quantité=3] [total=30] 
RegexMatchTimeoutException : recherche abandonnée au bout de 100 ms
NonBacktracking : False, réponse en moins d'une seconde : True

Comments:

  • Lines 39–51: Each template is declared by a partial static method ([partial]) with no body, which generates a [Regex], and is preceded by the attribute [GeneratedRegex]. The source generator writes the method body in another part of the class, which is also declared as [partial]. Starting with C# 13 and .NET 9, you can also declare a partial property: [[GeneratedRegex(...)] private static partial Regex Heure { get; }];
  • line 5: the method is used as a regular [Regex] object;
  • line 46: the second parameter of the attribute is a combination of options [RegexOptions]. [IgnoreCase] ignores case: “OUI” and “Yes” match the pattern;
  • line 17: the options are used in the same way with the methods of [Regex]. [Multiline] matches [^] and [$] at the beginning and end of each line in the string, rather than just at the beginning and end of the string itself. Other options are useful: [Singleline] ([.] also matches line breaks), [IgnorePatternWhitespace] (spaces in the pattern are ignored, allowing it to be written across multiple lines, including comments), [ExplicitCapture] (only named groups are remembered). These can be combined with the [|] operator;
  • line 50: the pattern [^(a+)+$] is pathological: when applied to a sequence of “a”s ending with another character, the regular expression engine tries every possible way to distribute the “a”s among the group repetitions before concluding that it has failed. The number of possibilities doubles with each additional “a”: with 30 “a”s, there are approximately one billion possibilities. This is known as a catastrophic backtracking. Such a pattern, when applied to strings entered by users, is a security vulnerability: just a few requests are enough to crash a server. The [matchTimeoutMilliseconds] parameter sets a timeout of 100 ms: after that, the search is abandoned with a [RegexMatchTimeoutException] exception (line 6);
  • line 35: the [NonBacktracking] option (.NET 7) uses a different engine, which guarantees a search time proportional to the string’s length. It does not support certain constructs (backward references, such as [\1], for example), but it returns a result immediately in this case.

Note that you must set a timeout or use [NonBacktracking] whenever the pattern or the string being searched comes from outside the program.

docs.title: 5.9. Example Application - V3
docs.text: We’ll revisit the application covered in Chapter 3 (Version 1) and Chapter 4 (Version 2). Remember that this is an exercise: the tax schedule used is the 2004 version (2003 income), which has remained unchanged since the original course.

docs.title: 5.9.1. Data in a File
docs.text:
In version 2, the tax calculation was performed in the abstract class [AbstractImpot], which we reproduce here unchanged, except for its namespace:

namespace ImpotsV3;

public abstract class AbstractImpot : IImpot
{
     // the tax brackets needed for the calculation come from an external source
     // known only to derived classes
    protected abstract TrancheImpot[] TranchesImpot { get; }

     // tax calculation
    public int Calculer(bool marie, int nbEnfants, int salaire)
    {
         // calculation of the number of shares
        decimal nbParts = (decimal)nbEnfants / 2 + (marie ? 2 : 1);
        if (nbEnfants >= 3)
        {
            nbParts += 0.5m;
        }
         // Calculation of taxable income and the family quotient
        decimal revenu = 0.72m * salaire;
        decimal quotient = revenu / nbParts;
         // Determination of the tax bracket: the last one is used if no other bracket applies
        TrancheImpot[] tranches = TranchesImpot;
        TrancheImpot tranche = tranches[^1];
        for (int i = 0; i < tranches.Length - 1; i++)
        {
            if (quotient <= tranches[i].Limite)
            {
                tranche = tranches[i];
                break;
            }
        }
         // tax calculation
        return (int)(revenu * tranche.CoeffR - nbParts * tranche.CoeffN);
    }
}

The [Calculer] method uses the tax brackets returned by the abstract property [TranchesImpot] (line 7). The [AbstractImpot] class does not know where these brackets come from: it is up to the derived classes to provide them. In version 2, the derived class [HardwiredImpot] hard-coded them into its code. A tax bracket is represented, as in version 2, by the record structure [TrancheImpot]:

namespace ImpotsV3;

// a tax bracket from the tax scale
public readonly record struct TrancheImpot(decimal Limite, decimal CoeffR, decimal CoeffN);

and the calculation is described by the interface [IImpot]:

namespace ImpotsV3;

public interface IImpot
{
     // Calculation of a taxpayer’s tax
    int Calculer(bool marie, int nbEnfants, int salaire);
}

The new version stores the data in a file, which allows you to change the pay scale without recompiling the program. We write two new classes derived from [AbstractImpot]:

  • [FileImpot] reads the brackets from a text file [DataImpot.txt];
  • [JsonImpot] reads them from a file named JSON and [DataImpot.json].

The text file [DataImpot.txt] contains one segment per line, in the format limit:coeffR:coeffN:

4962:0:0
8382:0.068:291.09
14753:0.191:1322.92
23888:0.283:2668.39
38868:0.374:4846.98
47932:0.426:6883.66
0:0.481:9505.54

The 2008 course wrote numbers with a decimal comma (0.068) and read them using [decimal.TryParse] in the machine’s locale: the same file, when read on a British or American machine, would have been rejected or, worse, misinterpreted. A data file must not depend on the language of the machine reading it: we write numbers with a decimal point and read them in the invariant culture ([CultureInfo.InvariantCulture]), which is also used by JSON and most data formats.

The file [DataImpot.json] contains the same data, in the form of a JSON array of objects:

[
  { "limite": 4962, "coeffR": 0, "coeffN": 0 },
  { "limite": 8382, "coeffR": 0.068, "coeffN": 291.09 },
  { "limite": 14753, "coeffR": 0.191, "coeffN": 1322.92 },
  { "limite": 23888, "coeffR": 0.283, "coeffN": 2668.39 },
  { "limite": 38868, "coeffR": 0.374, "coeffN": 4846.98 },
  { "limite": 47932, "coeffR": 0.426, "coeffN": 6883.66 },

docs.title: 5.9.2. Errors
docs.text:
Processing these files may fail: missing file, malformed line, incorrect number, etc. As in the 2008 version, we create a special exception class to report these errors. The 2008 course called it [FileImpotException]; we’re naming it [ImpotException], since it will also be used for other data sources (the JSON file here, and a database later). It carries an error code:

namespace ImpotsV3;

// error codes: powers of 2, which can be combined
[Flags]
public enum CodeErreur
{
    Acces = 1,      // The file cannot be read
    Ligne = 2,      // A row does not have three fields
    Champ1 = 4,     // Field 1 (limit) is incorrect
    Champ2 = 8,     // Field 2 (coeffR) is incorrect
    Champ3 = 16,    // Field 3 (coeffN) is incorrect
    Json = 32       // The document JSON is incorrect
}

// The exception thrown by the classes that read the tax brackets
public class ImpotException : Exception
{
     // the error code (a combination of values CodeErreur)
    public int Code { get; init; }

    public ImpotException(string message) : base(message) { }
    public ImpotException(string message, Exception inner) : base(message, inner) { }
}

Comments:

  • lines 16–22: The class [ImpotException] derives from the class [Exception]. It will be used to report any errors that occur while processing the data file. It has two constructors: the first takes an error message, and the second also takes the exception that caused the error, which will be available in the [InnerException] property;
  • Line 19: The property [Code] stores the error code. The keyword [init] allows this to be set only when the object is created, using an object initializer: [new ImpotException("...") { Code = 2 }]. It is this form of exception, with an integer code, that subsequent versions of the application will use;
  • lines 4–12: a list of possible error codes:
    • [Acces]: error accessing the data file;
    • [Ligne]: row missing the three expected fields, or file containing no segments;
    • [Champ1], [Champ2], [Champ3]: Field 1, 2, or 3 in a row is incorrect;
    • [Json]: The document JSON is incorrect.

Some of these errors may occur in combination: all three fields in a row may be incorrect. Therefore, the enumeration [CodeErreur] has been annotated with the attribute [Flags], and its values are powers of 2: each corresponds to a bit of the integer. An error in fields 2 and 3 will result in the code [Champ2 | Champ3], which is 8 + 16 = 24. Thanks to the [Flags] attribute, the [ToString] method of the enumeration displays such a combination in the form “Field2, Field3.”

docs.title: 5.9.3. The FileImpot class
docs.text:
The [FileImpot] class provides the segments read from a text file:

using System.Globalization;
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;

namespace ImpotsV3;

// the tax brackets read from a text file of lines delimited by:coeffR:coeffN
public partial class FileImpot : AbstractImpot
{
     // the field separator: the character: surrounded by spaces if present
    [GeneratedRegex(@"\s*:\s*")]
    private static partial Regex Separateur();

     // tax brackets read from the file
    private readonly TrancheImpot[] tranchesImpot;

     // Implementation of the parent class’s abstract property
    protected override TrancheImpot[] TranchesImpot => tranchesImpot;

    public FileImpot(string nomFichier)
    {
         // the filename (without the path) for error messages
        string nom = Path.GetFileName(nomFichier);
         // the tax brackets read; their number is unknown in advance
        List<TrancheImpot> tranches = [];
        try
        {
            int numLigne = 0;
            foreach (string ligneLue in File.ReadLines(nomFichier))
            {
                numLigne++;
                string ligne = ligneLue.Trim();
                 // empty lines are ignored
                if (ligne == "")
                {
                    continue;
                }
                 // the line must have three fields
                string[] champs = Separateur().Split(ligne);
                if (champs.Length != 3)
                {
                    throw new ImpotException($"Ligne n° {numLigne} incorrecte ({ligne})")
                    {
                        Code = (int)CodeErreur.Ligne
                    };
                }
                 // three positive or zero decimal numbers, written with a decimal point
                CodeErreur code = 0;
                if (!Lire(champs[0], out decimal limite)) code |= CodeErreur.Champ1;
                if (!Lire(champs[1], out decimal coeffR)) code |= CodeErreur.Champ2;
                if (!Lire(champs[2], out decimal coeffN)) code |= CodeErreur.Champ3;
                if (code != 0)
                {
                    throw new ImpotException($"Ligne n° {numLigne} incorrecte ({ligne})")
                    {
                        Code = (int)code
                    };
                }
                 // the new tax bracket is stored
                tranches.Add(new TrancheImpot(limite, coeffR, coeffN));
            }
        }
        catch (Exception e) when (e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)
        {
             // File access error: wrap it in a ImpotException
            throw new ImpotException($"Erreur lors de la lecture du fichier {nom}", e)
            {
                Code = (int)CodeErreur.Acces
            };
        }
         // At least one tax bracket is required
        if (tranches.Count == 0)
        {
            throw new ImpotException($"Le fichier {nom} ne contient aucune tranche")
            {
                Code = (int)CodeErreur.Ligne
            };
        }
         // Transfer the list to the tax bracket array
        tranchesImpot = tranches.ToArray();
    }

     // Converting a field to a decimal value >= 0, regardless of the machine's locale
    private static bool Lire(string champ, out decimal valeur) =>
        decimal.TryParse(champ, NumberStyles.AllowDecimalPoint, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out valeur);
}

Comments:

  • Line 7: The class [FileImpot] is derived from the class [AbstractImpot], just as the class [HardwiredImpot] was in version 2. It is declared as [partial] because it contains a generated regular expression;
  • lines 10–11: the regular expression for the field separator in a boundary line: coeffR:coeffN: the character [:], preceded and followed by any number of spaces;
  • lines 14–17: the read chunks, returned by the property [TranchesImpot], which redefines the abstract property of [AbstractImpot];
  • line 19: the constructor receives the name of the text file containing the data. Its role is to populate the array [tranchesImpot];
  • line 22: the file name without its path, used in error messages. The constructor actually receives a full path, which does not need to be displayed to the user;
  • line 24: Reading a text file is sequential: the number of lines is not known until the entire file has been read. Therefore, the array cannot be sized in advance; the chunks are temporarily stored in a list;
  • line 28: The file is read line by line using [File.ReadLines], which opens and closes the file itself. The 2008 course used [StreamReader];
  • lines 38–43: The line is split into fields using a regular expression; if there are not three fields, a [ImpotException] exception with code [Ligne] is thrown. The 2008 course stored the error in a variable, exited the loop, and then threw the exception after closing the file: throwing it immediately is simpler, and [File.ReadLines] closes the file in any case, since the loop [foreach] releases its counter even when an exception interrupts it;
  • lines 47–55: conversion of the three fields to decimal numbers. Errors are accumulated in the variable [code] using the operator [|=], then reported together;
  • lines 83–84: conversion of a field. [NumberStyles.AllowDecimalPoint] allows only digits and a decimal point: no signs, spaces, or thousands separators. Negative numbers are therefore rejected, which validates the data at the same time as it is converted. [CultureInfo.InvariantCulture] enforces the period as the decimal separator, regardless of the machine’s locale;
  • lines 62–67: file access errors ([IOException] and its variants, such as [FileNotFoundException], or [UnauthorizedAccessException] for insufficient permissions) are wrapped in a [ImpotException] with code [Acces]. The [when (...)] exception filter (C# 6) intercepts only these exceptions: [ImpotException] exceptions thrown within the loop are not intercepted and exit the constructor unchanged. The pattern [e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException] is a pattern of type combined by [or] (C# 9);
  • lines 71–79: an empty file is rejected; otherwise, the list is transferred to the slice array, which was the purpose of the constructor.

Encapsulating low-level exceptions ([IOException]) into an application-specific exception ([ImpotException]) allows the calling code to handle only one type of exception, regardless of the data source: a text file, a JSON file, and, later in the course, a database.

docs.title: 5.9.4. The JsonImpot class
docs.text:
The [JsonImpot] class provides the chunks read from a JSON file:

using System.Text.Json;

namespace ImpotsV3;

// tax brackets read from a file JSON
public class JsonImpot : AbstractImpot
{
     // "Web" options: property names in camelCase (limit, coeffR, coeffN)
    private static readonly JsonSerializerOptions options = new(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web);

     // tax brackets read from the file
    private readonly TrancheImpot[] tranchesImpot;

     // Implementation of the parent class's abstract property
    protected override TrancheImpot[] TranchesImpot => tranchesImpot;

    public JsonImpot(string nomFichier)
    {
         // the filename (without the path) for error messages
        string nom = Path.GetFileName(nomFichier);
        string json;
        try
        {
             // Reading the file
            json = File.ReadAllText(nomFichier);
        }
        catch (Exception e) when (e is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)
        {
            throw new ImpotException($"Erreur lors de la lecture du fichier {nom}", e)
            {
                Code = (int)CodeErreur.Acces
            };
        }
        TrancheImpot[]? tranches;
        try
        {
             // Deserialization of the slice array
            tranches = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<TrancheImpot[]>(json, options);
        }
        catch (JsonException e)
        {
            throw new ImpotException($"Le fichier {nom} est incorrect : {e.Message}", e)
            {
                Code = (int)CodeErreur.Json
            };
        }
         // At least one slice is required; negative values are not allowed
        if (tranches is null || tranches.Length == 0)
        {
            throw new ImpotException($"Le fichier {nom} ne contient aucune tranche")
            {
                Code = (int)CodeErreur.Json
            };
        }
        if (tranches.Any(t => t.Limite < 0 || t.CoeffR < 0 || t.CoeffN < 0))
        {
            throw new ImpotException($"Le fichier {nom} contient une valeur négative")
            {
                Code = (int)CodeErreur.Json
            };
        }
        tranchesImpot = tranches;
    }
}

Comments:

  • Line 9: The “Web” options: the properties JSON, [limite], [coeffR], and [coeffN] correspond to the properties [Limite], [CoeffR], and [CoeffN] in the [TrancheImpot] structure without needing to modify the latter with attributes. The options are stored in a static field: a [JsonSerializerOptions] object stores information about the types it has processed, and it is recommended to reuse it;
  • lines 25–31: reading the file; an access error is handled as in [FileImpot];
  • Line 38: A single instruction converts the text JSON into an array of slices. [System.Text.Json] knows how to construct a record structure by calling its constructor. An invalid document triggers a [JsonException], encapsulated within a [ImpotException] of code [Json];
  • lines 48–57: deserialization checks the document’s format, not the validity of the data: it remains to be verified that there is at least one segment (the document [null] or [] is a valid JSON) and that no values are negative. The method LINQ [Any] performs this final check in a single line.

Comparing the two classes is instructive: with a structured data format and a library that understands it, parsing the file no longer requires any code.

docs.title: 5.9.5. The main program
docs.text:
The [ImpotsV3] console project has the following directory structure:

05-classes-dotnet/
  05-classes-dotnet.slnx
  ImpotsV3/
    AbstractImpot.cs
    DataImpot.json
    DataImpot.txt
    DataImpotInvalide.json
    DataImpotInvalide.txt
    FileImpot.cs
    IImpot.cs
    ImpotException.cs
    ImpotsV3.csproj
    JsonImpot.cs
    Program.cs
    TrancheImpot.cs

The project file [ImpotsV3.csproj] is the one created by [dotnet new console], to which a group of elements has been added:

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
  </PropertyGroup>

   <!-- Data files are copied next to the executable -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <None Update="DataImpot*.txt;DataImpot*.json" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>

The element [<None Update="..." CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />] (line 12) specifies that the data files should be copied to the executable’s folder ([bin/Debug/net10.0]) during compilation if they are newer than the existing copy. The character [*] allows you to specify all [DataImpot*.txt] and [DataImpot*.json] files at once. This is equivalent to the “Copy to Output Directory” property that the 2008 course set in the file properties in Visual Studio.

The [Program.cs] program is as follows:

using ImpotsV3;

// Tax calculation, version 3: tax brackets are read from a file
// Syntax: dotnet run [-- fichier]; file: DataImpot.txt by default, or a .json file

const string syntaxe = """
    syntaxe : Marié NbEnfants Salaire
    Marié : o pour marié, n pour non marié
    NbEnfants : nombre d'enfants
    Salaire : salaire annuel en euros
    """;

// The data file is searched for next to the executable
string nomFichier = args.Length > 0 ? args[0] : "DataImpot.txt";
string chemin = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, nomFichier);
Console.WriteLine($"Tranches d'impôt lues dans [{nomFichier}]");

// creates a IImpot object; the class depends on the file extension
IImpot impot;
try
{
    impot = Path.GetExtension(nomFichier).ToLower() switch
    {
        ".json" => new JsonImpot(chemin),
        _ => new FileImpot(chemin)
    };
}
catch (ImpotException e)
{
     // Displaying the error; the code is displayed as a combination of CodeErreur
    string origine = e.InnerException is null ? "" : $", Exception d'origine : {e.InnerException.GetType().Name}";
    Console.WriteLine($"L'erreur suivante s'est produite : [Code={(CodeErreur)e.Code}, Message={e.Message}{origine}]");
     // program termination
    return 1;
}

// input loop
while (true)
{
     // Tax calculation parameters are requested
    Console.Write("Paramètres du calcul de l'impôt au format : Marié (o/n) NbEnfants Salaire ou rien pour arrêter : ");
    string parametres = (Console.ReadLine() ?? "").Trim();
     // Is there anything to do?
    if (parametres == "")
    {
        break;
    }
     // Checking the number of fields in the entered row
    string[] champs = parametres.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);
    if (champs.Length != 3)
    {
        Console.WriteLine(syntaxe);
        continue;
    }
     // Checking parameter validity
     // married
    string marie = champs[0].ToLower();
    if (marie != "o" && marie != "n")
    {
        Console.WriteLine(syntaxe + "\nArgument marié incorrect : tapez o ou n");
        continue;
    }
     // nbEnfants
    if (!int.TryParse(champs[1], out int nbEnfants) || nbEnfants < 0)
    {
        Console.WriteLine(syntaxe + "\nArgument NbEnfants incorrect : tapez un entier positif ou nul");
        continue;
    }
     // salary
    if (!int.TryParse(champs[2], out int salaire) || salaire < 0)
    {
        Console.WriteLine(syntaxe + "\nArgument salaire incorrect : tapez un entier positif ou nul");
        continue;
    }
     // Parameters are correct: calculate tax
    Console.WriteLine($"Impôt={impot.Calculer(marie == "o", nbEnfants, salaire)} euros");
}
return 0;

Comments:

  • line 14: the name of the data file is passed as an argument; by default, it is [DataImpot.txt];
  • line 15: the file is searched for in the executable’s folder, [AppContext.BaseDirectory], where it was copied during compilation. Thus, the program finds its data regardless of the folder from which it is launched, which was not the case for the single-file applications in this chapter;
  • Lines 22–25: An expression, [switch] (Chapter 3), selects the class to instantiate based on the file extension. The two branches return different types, [JsonImpot] and [FileImpot]: the compiler infers the type of the expression using the destination variable [impot], which is of type [IImpot] (expression [switch] with target type). The rest of the program only knows the interface [IImpot] and is unaware of where the data comes from;
  • lines 28–34: Creating the object may trigger a [ImpotException], which is displayed before the program terminates. The code is converted to [CodeErreur] to be displayed in plain text; the original exception, if any, is identified by its type (its message contains the full file path);
  • Lines 37–76: The dialog loop is exactly the same as in version 2.
